It took some time, but the paper has reached the stage of final draft. Thanks to all of your contributions so far!
We welcome all authors to carefully proofread the paper, which can be found here (pdf).

When proofreading, check for the usual ways to improve a paper (consistency, clarity and flow of the text).
There is also a separate checklist of additional things to consider when proofreading.

There are a few items on that list that still require fixes in many places:

  1. Use \subseteq for (non-strict) inequality on sets
  2. Use \le for (non-strict) inequality on cubes
  3. Add more links to Lean code (using \href + \extlink).
  4. Remove labels from equations that aren't referenced.

It would be great if volunteers claim one of these tasks, and incorporate them throughout the paper.

If you notice something in the paper that could be improved, please be bold and just open a PR suggesting a fix. If you don't know how to best improve something, you can also ask/discuss in this thread.

Since August is holiday time, I think it's good not to make this phase too short,
but let's also not let this go on indefinitely.
Let's set the deadline for this period at Friday, 4th of September (6 weeks from now).

I'll be on holiday myself for the next week.
I’ll probably have some time over the weekend, so I’m happy to take care of items 1–4 and go through the paper for those if it's ok with you.

Regarding:

  1. Remove labels from equations that aren't referenced.

Should we do the same for other unreferenced envs (e.g. sections)?

A bit late, but I went through it once more. I think in general it looks pretty good! I have added some small suggestions in a PR. Here are some bigger things that I wonder about:

  1. For some of the code snippets, it might still be nice to have a permalink to the repository or to mathlib
  2. At the end of section two, it says "Firstly, each theorem is a Lean definition ... auditing the same 170 lines as above". Here I am not completely sure what this is meant to say.
  3. "Again, in different context the existing mathlib ..." Here as well, I don't quite know what was meant here
  4. I wonder if the article should finish as it does, because the current end is quite technical, and maybe we want to close it off with a clearer message

Thanks everybody for your feedback! After some last proofreading rounds by Floris, María and me, I submitted the paper to the arXiv today (areas math.CA and CS.LO, MSC classification 42B20, 68V20). My understanding is that it will be publicly announced on Monday. I'll privately share the arXiv paper code with all authors then.
On Monday, I'll submit the paper to the Annals of Formalised Mathematics.

Note (since for some of you this might be your first arXiv paper): you might have gotten an email from a journal to submit your manuscript to a journal. Such emails are spam, and the senders are either scammers or predatory journals (or very low quality journals?).
they called me Dr. :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes: (which i am not)
They call me professor, which wasn't true even when I was working at a university.
The preprint is 2609.31334; I just DMed everybody the password. And the preprint is submitted now.
You can use the password to claim the paper as yours by logging in to arXiv (creating an account if you don't have one) and going here: https://arxiv.org/auth/need-paper-password
